This paper presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the limited pitch control of WaveNet (WN) through pitch-dependent dilated convolution neural networks. WN achieves high-fidelity audio generation using stacked dilated convolution layers as an autoregressive probabilistic model. However, the lack of prior knowledge and the pure data-driven nature of WN lead to pitch control difficulties, particularly in modeling periodic signal components for inputs outside the training frequency range. To overcome this challenge, QPNet is proposed with two innovations. Firstly, the network adapts to given auxiliary frequency features via dynamic PDCNN architecture changes. Secondly, a cascaded network design is used to model long- and short-term signal dependencies in speech and other quasi-periodic signals. Experimental evaluations of QPNet demonstrate the benefits of PDCNNs for unseen frequency inputs and the cascaded structure's effectiveness in modeling speech waveforms. Code for QPNet is publicly available at https://github.com/ParandMinigha/Quasi-Periodic-WaveNet.

Our primary goal in this research is to pinpoint sound sources within video frames without relying on manually labeled data. Our core innovation involves training the network to distinguish between difficult image elements, including those that include the object generating the sound, to significantly enhance sound source localization performance. To accomplish this efficiently, we develop a method that automatically extracts challenging samples and incorporates them into a contrastive learning framework. Our algorithm achieves superior results on the Flickr SoundNet dataset, a prominent benchmark. Moreover, we introduce a new dataset called VGG-Sound Source, a comprehensive set of annotated video clips featuring sound sources with explicit bounding box markings. VGG-Sound Source surpasses existing datasets in scale, size, and category diversity, consisting of 5,000 videos spanning over 200 categories. Notably, it differs from Flickr SoundNet in that it is based on video data. Our algorithm also demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on this new dataset when compared to several baseline methods. Our code is available at github.com/fchong86/sound-source-localization.

By integrating the minimal dark sector into the simplest "missing partner" type-I seesaw framework, we establish a comprehensive understanding of neutrino oscillation lengths. Here, the "atmospheric" mass scale is directly produced at tree level, whereas the "solar" scale arises through radiative processes, mediated by the dark sector. Furthermore, we determine the parameter ranges that meet theoretical requirements, in addition to dark matter relic abundance and direct detection standards. Consequently, we derive a minimum threshold for the neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude. Lastly, we investigate the interplay between the dark matter phenomenon and the Higgs vacuum stability, revealing the influence of the Higgs self-coupling on the neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude and identifying the minimal parameter configurations that avoid the electroweak vacuum instability and ensure the stability of the vacuum in the "solar" sector. Specifically, it investigates the properties of relative I-functions in the context of toric complete intersections. For a particular example, a particular class of I-functions is identified. Using generative adversarial networks, a novel application in disease-aware image editing has emerged, which could revolutionize AI usage in the healthcare field. In this research, a concept for GAN-based medical imaging enhancement is demonstrated. Though GAN-based techniques excel at natural image creation and manipulation, their potential in medicine remains largely unexplored. Our research utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. By incorporating an encoder from the Cyclic Reverse Generator framework, we successfully developed an inverse mapping system to recreate synthetic X-rays accurately and reconstruct organs on real X-rays. By fine-tuning latent codes, we successfully transplanted a cardiac enlargement condition onto normal chest X-rays. Our research was showcased at the Medical Imaging meets NeurIPS Workshop 2020, a satellite event of the 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems held in Vancouver, Canada. Our investigation utilized the CheXpert dataset to train a StyleGAN that effectively produces authentic chest X-rays. Though the findings are promising, there are limitations to overcome before using this technology on real patients. Our research highlighted the potential of GAN-based image editing for medical applications, but stress the importance of verifying the accuracy of edited organs and structures, and the need to account for variations in imaging protocols when working with real-world data. ViDaExpert is an application for multidimensional data visualization and
advanced analysis. It is capable of handling object-feature tables that include
numerical values and text-based labels for objects and features. The tool
encompasses several statistical techniques such as weighted PCA, elastic maps,
linear discriminant analysis, and decision tree construction, in addition to
K-Means clustering and multilinear regression. With customizable visualizations
and an interactive 3D viewer, ViDaExpert enables the creation of 3D scenes
from data and facilitates rapid, in-depth analysis of data, encompassing
elementary to complex methodologies. The application is particularly suitable
for research in biology and medicine, where data often involves high-dimensional
vectorial data. The application, developed using Java, is accessible on
Unix/Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows platforms. An executable version of
ViDaExpert is available for download, along with sample datasets and an
illustrative tutorial. The application's source code is also available within
